## Independent deep review: #30679

Audited `b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f`. Three concrete counterexamples refine the original buffering plan; no audio/device run was performed.

### P1 — A corrected final frame can be silently discarded while marked final (reproduced)

Executed `/tmp/guardian-project19-deep-review/probe-30679.ts` with Bun. It extracts the unchanged production `queueAssistantSpeech` callback and real text-boundary/remainder helpers; collaborators capture tasks instead of playing audio. For the same message ID:

1. Streaming frame `The available option is red.` queues that sentence.
2. Final frame `Actually, the available option is blue.` queues **nothing**.
3. State records `latestSpeakable` as the corrected final, `queuedSpeakablePrefix` as the stale red sentence, and `finalQueued:true`.

[remainderAfter](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-playback.ts#L185-L207) returns empty when prior text is not a prefix/interior substring; the [consumer](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2816-L2829) treats that as no remaining speech and marks completion. The original plan must specify a non-monotonic stream contract, not only buffer sizes. Do not blindly replay the full final (duplicates already spoken words); distinguish queued-but-unplayed text, actual played content, and replacement/correction events. Reject unsupported rewrites explicitly or deliver a deliberate corrected utterance with clear ownership.

Second actual probe: `Hello there.` → final `Note: Hello there. More.` queues only `Hello there.` and `More.`. Interior-substring recovery drops `Note:` but records the whole final as queued. Remove silent interior matching; acceptance must compare the actual delivered text sequence against the authorized append/revision contract.

These are deterministic boundary counterexamples, not proof that every production provider rewrites text. Current shell [provisional-frame suppression](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/components/shell/useShellVoiceOutput.ts#L175-L186) specifically protects one known wholesale-replacement path and must remain. Other callers, direct hook use, and non-provisional replacement still require a defined contract.

### P2 — Monotonic text alone does not make chunk boundaries pronounceable (reproduced)

Actual callback probe: partial `I am checking the international` followed by final `I am checking the internationalization settings.` queues two independent requests: `I am checking the international` and `ization settings.`. The [threshold branch](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2831-L2842) sends the entire partial string once it exceeds 24 characters, even when the final word may still be streaming. The debounce flush has the same unresolved trailing-word problem at lines 2669–2706. This is an exact request segmentation defect; no specific acoustic measurement is claimed.

Amend prefetch work to retain an unfinished lexical suffix until a stable delimiter or final event, with language-aware handling where spaces are not word boundaries. A timer does not prove word completion. Preserve all characters and ordering; do not use a maximum-length truncation to repair prosody. Test token streams split inside words, Unicode graphemes, decimal numbers, abbreviations and URLs, then inspect real spoken continuity on supported targets.

### P2 — Latency improvement must separate synthesis scheduling from playback completion

The [worker](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/hooks/useVoiceChat.ts#L2382-L2532) awaits each provider's full speak operation. [Decoded playback](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/b676280384b15df54204276e34bb8740db26936f/packages/ui/src/voice/voice-chat-audio-playback.ts#L130-L168) resolves on completion/timeout. Thus a later clip is synthesized only after earlier playback finishes on the buffered local/ElevenLabs path; faster segmentation alone cannot hide that synthesis interval. Implement bounded prefetch with one ordered playback owner and cancelable generation. Bound retained audio bytes/concurrency, not text completeness.

### Examined protections, ownership and acceptance amendments

Decoded playback checks generation both before and after asynchronous decode (`voice-chat-audio-playback.ts` lines 65–67); do not allege a missing decode cancellation guard. `cancelPlayback` increments generation, clears queue, aborts active fetch, and completes the playback waiter; retain all four when prefetch adds multiple requests. Reject late prefetched audio for old generations and test cancellation during synthesis, decode, and playback. Provider failure already fails closed. Coordinate the queue configuration/key race with #30680 so prefetch cannot synthesize one voice and label/cache another.

The shell message watcher explicitly exits for Cartesia realtime (`useShellVoiceOutput.ts` lines 147–151). This report's buffered-path findings must not be presented as a diagnosis of realtime Sonic. Live GitHub inspection confirms #29492 remains OPEN/DRAFT at `b209c79fe2ac1bde176204f078834f9352b8395c`; reusing its work requires exact-head review, not assuming it is merged. HEAD's #30723 changes native HTTP stream metadata validation; it does not repair these queue/text boundaries.

Require evidence for the exact target/provider reproducing the user's symptom: full authorized text vs queued/synthesized/played intervals, first-audio time, inter-clip silence, final-frame arrival, cancellation outcome, and subjective playback review. Pure task-capture probes above establish text loss/splitting but cannot establish acoustic latency or native playback success.

### Independent long-reply finding and repair in progress

The human listening acceptance above applies to the exact short recordings. A separate live navigation test exposed a longer reply ending mid-sentence: 180 words of generated text produced 22.6 seconds of Kokoro audio, and independent ASR found only 87 spoken words. The standalone scheduler passed the entire reply as one phrase; the native Kokoro tokenizer silently retained only its first 510 phoneme tokens.

The repair preflights every segment of the complete utterance before synthesis, splits at word boundaries while preserving ordered text, rejects an indivisible oversized word before emitting a prefix, and sends the same checked IPA to the native ABI v14+ IPA entry. Old libraries without that entry and exhausted audio allocations return explicit errors. Cancellation prevents later segment dispatch.

The exact captured reply now produces 43.875 seconds of real Kokoro audio (SHA-256 `4f335c87ec0087d0c33a79f92df4c94ff26d6c2e279a6ba42bb5eb080f2806ab`). The full inference suite passed 2,916 tests across 282 files plus 60 native harness tests; 19 tests were explicitly skipped. Typecheck and lint passed. Independent review then found a separator-only suffix could produce empty IPA after a valid prefix; follow-up `9564979b97` rejects it during complete preflight, with 29 focused tests passing. Follow-up independent review found no remaining actionable defect and independently passed all 29 boundary tests plus the installed-phonemizer adversarial probe. Final root validation remains pending. This is recorded-audio proof, not microphone or all-provider acceptance.

**Describe the bug**

The English UI renders the *names* of 37 translation keys instead of their text. The character editor's unsaved-changes dialog is titled "Unsaved Changes Title" with the body "Unsaved Changes Body"; its counts read "3 Conversation Count" and "2 Post Count"; the computer-use approval overlay's title is "Title", its body "Body", its mode line "Mode Line"; the browser workspace's blocked-frame card says "Frame Blocked Title" / "Frame Blocked Description"; a dialog button reads "Dont Save".

Two things combine on `origin/develop` (`1045297cca`):

1. `packages/ui/src/i18n/index.ts:48` resolves `localized[key] ?? english[key] ?? defaultValue ?? key`, so the catalog value in `locales/en.json` always wins over the `defaultValue` the call site passes. That is by design (the catalog is the source of truth), and `check-i18n.mjs` enforces that every literal key is catalogued.
2. When the catalog was backfilled, these 37 keys were catalogued with their own Title-Cased key name as the value — `"charactereditor.UnsavedChangesTitle": "Unsaved Changes Title"` — while every call site passes the real English as `defaultValue`. Because of (1), the real English never renders.

# Risks

Medium: introduces a credential-bearing API boundary and a separate product's Stripe operations. Routes require a registered app and hashed client secret. User delegation is short-lived, revocable, and checked against primary account authority; Google ownership remains enforced by the managed connector service. Billing validates app/workspace/customer/price metadata and verifies Stripe webhook signatures. All new routes remain unavailable until explicit Outreachr bindings are configured.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Outreachr can exchange its existing app-login code for scoped identity and managed Google access without copying Google credentials into the CRM. The primary database retains an authorization-code digest so replay stays blocked even after grant revocation or a stale cache read. Google transport permits only the Gmail/calendar operations used by the CRM.

The billing boundary reuses Cloud's Stripe service for separate Outreachr workspace customers and monthly seat prices. Stable idempotency keys protect customer and checkout creation; current subscriptions are read from Stripe and webhooks are signature-verified. Existing Cloud products and subscriptions are not changed.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature; additive backend routes and an append-only delegation migration.

# Documentation changes needed?

Deployment bindings and migration order are documented in the companion Outreachr cloud README and implementation plan. Apply `0376_outreachr_delegations.sql` before enabling the routes; configure the exact app ID/origin/client-secret digest plus Sol/Astra price IDs and a dedicated webhook secret. Use the standard staging certification and production approval workflow.

`outreachr-delegation.test.ts`, `outreachr-billing.test.ts`, and `outreachr-delegations-migration.pglite.test.ts` under `packages/cloud/shared/src`.

95:T49bf,## Summary

This PR consolidates the independently executable duplicate systems identified by the repository-wide audit in #30125. It establishes one executable owner for each migrated behavior, leaves host/platform policy in thin adapters, adds parity or provenance checks around compatibility paths, and preserves the boundaries that are intentionally separate (providers, connectors, auth domains, storage tenancy, platform I/O, generated output, and vendored code).

The highest-risk changes are deliberately structured around canonical kernels rather than broad package mergers:

- runtime/config contracts now execute from `@elizaos/core`, with stable `@elizaos/shared` paths acting as compatibility facades;
- dependency-light config input validation lives in shared, while agent-only defaults are applied in an explicit materialization step;
- LifeOps carve-outs use durable receipts so deleted data is not silently resurrected;
- UI and runtime local-inference selection use the same typed recommendation policy;
- Cloud/local MCP, registry, gateway routing, retry timing, frontmatter, native HTTP, screen capture, host routes, training staging, and quantization now share inward kernels with target-specific adapters;
- data-bearing or native-source duplicates that cannot be deleted safely without live or ABI evidence are guarded and surfaced rather than silently discarded.

Closes #30125.

## Additional consolidation and drift prevention

The same ownership rules are applied to medium-risk exact clones and meta-systems touched by the implementation:

- AES-256-GCM token-at-rest behavior moves to the Node core utility, with finances/health compatibility exports and ciphertext/key-file/environment tests.
- Integration observability becomes a shared event/span contract with agent/app-core policy adapters.
- Voice settings share one UI controller while local/device and Cloud panels keep capability-specific rendering.
- Real-runtime Vitest configuration, native Capacitor/Rollup scaffolding, template cleanup scripts, static assets, and nested workflow templates are generated or manifest-checked instead of hand-copied.
- Cloud migration prefixes gain a total-order manifest and duplicate-prefix check without renaming historical migrations.
- Provider and connector account plumbing gains authoring/conformance helpers while preserving provider/channel implementations.

## Data migration, security, and compatibility

### Relationships

This change does **not** guess that a retired data store is empty. The active graph remains `KnowledgeGraphService`; startup inventory reports whether legacy `app_relationships` tables exist and whether they contain rows. Empty legacy tables may be retired safely. A non-empty inventory is a hard migration decision: rows must be imported with identity, redirect, merge, and evidence preservation before the old schema can be dropped. No destructive DDL is introduced here.

### LifeOps carve-outs

The common migration runner writes a durable `app_eliza_migrations.carve_out_receipts` record keyed by domain migration. It uses a holder token and recoverable lease, marks completion only after the domain callback succeeds, and releases its own lease on failure. Completed receipts prevent a later empty target table from being interpreted as “never migrated,” which is the stale-source resurrection failure this work is intended to close. Domain callbacks remain responsible for explicit columns, validation, repairs, and sensitive-field scrubbing.

### Secrets and untrusted boundaries

- Token encryption preserves the existing AES-256-GCM ciphertext and key discovery contract; adapters do not log plaintext, keys, or provider payloads.
- MCP schemas and model-produced JSON are budgeted and validated in an isolated boundary; Cloud OAuth/tool visibility and local transport authorization remain host policies.
- Registry URLs/wire records are normalized before use; registry cache fallback remains explicit rather than fabricating healthy data.
- Native HTTP and capture contracts validate/normalize crossing data while preserving exact bytes, bodyless statuses, timestamps, dimensions, and formats.
- Gateway discovery retains bounded stale-ring behavior and authenticated Kubernetes discovery; connector identity/auth and forwarded-host policy stay outside the generic hash kernel.
- Retry code centralizes timing and disposal mechanics without granting replay permission to unsafe non-idempotent requests.

## Rollback plan

Rollback is by ownership family, not by deleting user data:

1. Revert an adapter to its prior implementation while leaving new shared kernels present; stable import paths and public wrappers are preserved for this purpose.
2. Do not delete durable carve-out receipts during rollback. Their presence is the safety record that prevents stale legacy rows from being re-imported.
3. Do not drop `app_relationships` on rollback or deployment. If the inventory reports rows, stop and run an evidence-preserving migration before any retirement change.
4. Native integrated copies and public training wrapper commands remain available, so provenance/kernel adoption can be reverted without changing artifact names or ABI inputs.
5. Cloud gateway/retry/MCP rollbacks retain connector-specific auth, OAuth, identity, and routing policy in the host adapters; no credential or tenancy migration is required.

## Guarantees

- production is Linux-only and descriptor-bound through `/proc/self/fd`; every traversed directory is opened `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`

- non-Linux pathname emulation is available only with the explicit test-only flag under `NODE_ENV=test`; production fails closed

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first tranche of the canonical invite-to-ready group installation lifecycle (#23107):

1. **Durable provider-neutral state machine** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-lifecycle.ts`): an account-scoped installation record joining provider invite, external group, required scopes, single-use expiring owner claim, runtime room binding, readiness state, removal, and reinstall versioning. States: `invite_created → provider_authorized → agent_joined → permissions_verifying → owner_claim_pending → ready`, with terminal `degraded`/`removed`/`revoked`/`failed`. Signed-event normalization: events are tenant-bound, idempotent, replay-safe (terminal receipt replay is a no-op), and epoch-guarded (future `reinstallVersion` epochs rejected; stale epochs rejected; equal-epoch reapply rejects wrong-secret attempts and persists attempt burning to exhaustion).
2. **Connector contribution contract** (`packages/core/src/messaging/installation-contribution.ts` + `installation-service.ts`): the contract a connector implements — install/deep-link shape, group types, scope requirements, signed event normalization, readiness proof, uninstall, provider-specific activation. `InstallationLifecycleService` registers contributions per `(agentId, connectorId)`.
3. **Discord pilot adapter** (`plugins/plugin-discord/installation-adapter.ts`, `discord-events.ts`, `index.ts`, `messages.ts`): canonical permission catalog (tiered invite URL activation), guildCreate/guildDelete normalization (unknown shapes refused), owner-claim handoff that never exposes tokens in the group, and the gateway-boundary fence — a fenced (removed/revoked/failed) guild skips `handleGuildCreate` at the event-listener seam and stops message traffic at the message-send seam.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality).

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation (contract is documented in code headers; user-facing install UX arrives with the next tranche's install-URL surface).

Refs #29967.

## Ordering invariant

Every covered path follows validate -> one standing snapshot -> durable admission -> dispatch marker -> provider -> deferred settlement. Malformed, unauthorized, unavailable, or bad-standing requests dispatch nothing. After dispatch, provider uncertainty settles conservatively; status/cache updates run through `waitUntil` and do not read the cache back.

The trusted inbound-vision webhook has no credential key, so its standing check is one synchronous combined SQL decision in the existing claim/quota transaction rather than a credential-keyed KV read. Its completion/failure settlement is one fenced asynchronous UPDATE with no SELECT or RETURNING.

# Risks

Medium. Enrollment advances sandbox schedule state and creates durable backup work. A defect could skip due work, duplicate queue entries, cross a source occurrence, or strand a shard. The repository therefore uses one atomic transaction, frozen per-shard cohort authority, bounded disjoint candidate frontiers, exact source revalidation, deterministic organization locking, and replay-safe insertion.

# What does this PR do?

- Leases one of 64 durable enrollment shards with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, preferring incomplete cohorts.
- Freezes the database cutoff, snapshot xid, RPO, cohort identity, and keyset cursor for resumable enrollment.
- Selects three disjoint due frontiers, each bounded at `limit + 1`, then globally orders and caps the result.
- Revalidates active organization lifecycle and exact sandbox/node occurrence authority before mutation.
- Atomically advances `next_backup_at`, enrollment cursors, queued `schedule_capture` / `reserve_capture` work, and shard progress.
- Inserts exact replay identities with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; queued rows begin with attempts `0`, no lease, and no claim proof.
- Performs database admission mutations only. It has no provider, provisioning, capacity, autoscale, or restore dependency.

a7:T1b8b,feat(core): durable per-principal capability grants, slice 1 (#23102)

## Summary

First implementation slice for #23102 per the issue's own slicing guidance: a durable subject × capability × resource grant store and the canonical fail-closed `authorizeCapability` decision path, in a new `packages/core/src/features/capabilities/` module. Storage lives in a dedicated `capabilities` Postgres schema, self-materialized through idempotent DDL on first store use (the TrajectoriesService pattern) because no registered plugin carries a schema-bearing entry — relying on plugin-schema migration would leave the tables uncreated in real deployments.

- **Typed, versioned vocabulary** (`types.ts`): canonical subjects (`entity:<uuid>`, `role:<name>`, `world:<uuid>`, case-folded), dot-separated lowercase capabilities, strict selector grammar (`*`, exact ids, trailing `/*` only — printable ASCII allowlist, no leading/trailing/double slashes, length cap). Malformed input is rejected at the write (error-policy J3); legacy rows that drift are quarantined — visible for management, never authoritative.
- **Store** (`CapabilityGrantStore.ts`): validated create, version-checked update, idempotent revoke — each mutation and its global `capability_epoch` bump commit in ONE transaction; a missing epoch singleton rolls the mutation back instead of fabricating progress. Uncapped live-grant reads filtered (expiry `> now`, non-revoked) in SQL. Concurrent-safe promise-memoized DDL bootstrap.
- **Decision path** (`authorizeCapability.ts`): fixed evaluation order — validate (fail closed) → explicit deny grants → allow grants (constraints intersected: numeric min, typed scalar array intersection, structural equality; incompatible → deny) → role-tier composition hook → deny `NO_MATCHING_GRANT` (no implicit allow). No decision cache, so revocation is effective before the next call returns by construction. Every decision attempts exactly one audit row (id generated up front); audit failures are reported through an injected `onAuditFailure` hook (J7; wire to `runtime.reportError` at the boundary) and can never block or flip a decision. Audit rows carry categorical/sanitized fields only — raw malformed values and driver errors never enter the log.
- **Enforcement inventory** (`capability-boundary-inventory.ts`): 12 privileged boundaries (message send/read, device, fs read/write, PTy, git, media read/write, provider invoke, admin API, coding environments) with per-boundary status; the shape is test-validated. Completeness against future repo boundaries is a human-review obligation until the slice-2 classifier.
- Exported node-only from `index.node.ts` (SQL-bound; browser/edge untouched).

## Test evidence

`bun run --cwd packages/core test` scope: **41/41 passing** real-PGlite tests in `CapabilityGrantStore.test.ts` (default vitest lane; PGlite disk data dirs, real Drizzle queries, no mocks of the system under test):

- Self-migration from an empty database; concurrent first calls share one bootstrap
- Restart survival: handle closed, fresh handle opened on the SAME disk dir — grants (and deny grants) created under the first handle remain authoritative; epoch identical
- Revocation visible to the very next decision; expiry boundary `expiresAt <= now` never matches
- Deny-wins over simultaneous allows and over the role tier; role tier never rescues a deny; broken resolver degrades to deny
- Fail-closed: malformed subject/capability/agentId/resource/worldId → `INVALID_REQUEST`; store down → `STORE_UNAVAILABLE`; no grant → `NO_MATCHING_GRANT`
- Audit: per-decision rows, categorical details (raw values withheld), 512-char resource truncation, failure reported through the hook, throwing reporter cannot abort any decision path
- Optimistic-version conflicts; partial unique index (world-aware via nil-uuid coalescing) blocks duplicate active policies and frees on revoke; identical policies legal in distinct worlds and alongside global
- Typed constraint intersection incl. non-scalar arrays → incompatible; nearest expiry across multiple allows
- Quarantine of legacy rows with malformed selector/issuer/capability/subject/effect/provenance
- Mutation rollback when the epoch singleton is missing (zero grant rows survive)
- Boundary inventory shape validation

Typecheck clean (`bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck`), Biome clean, `bun run --cwd packages/core build` succeeds and the built barrel exports `authorizeCapability` + store API (verified by import probe against the built output).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Implements the first production slice of #23103:

1. **Pin/unpin/list through service + REST + agent action.** `DocumentService.setDocumentPinned` performs a CAS-protected metadata mutation through the existing authorization + revision fencing plus the dedicated `expectedPinned` pin-bit fence (review r1: two racing pin writers from the same observed state now serialize — exactly one `updated`, the loser gets a typed conflict and the service's bounded retry converges against fresh state; no second write path). REST: `POST /api/documents/:id/pin` / `DELETE /api/documents/:id/pin` behind the existing mutate gate, mapping typed `DOCUMENT_PIN_UNSUPPORTED` to 503. Agent surface: `pin`/`unpin` subactions on the DOCUMENT umbrella action. The presented-document wire shape now carries `pinned`, and the Documents view shows a visible per-row pending state with a fail-closed unsupported-adapter signal.
2. **Post-#24134 prompt-integrity policy on pinned provider injection.** The deterministic 8,000-token pinned-injection cap (first-N selection + `[PINNED KNOWLEDGE TRUNCATED]` marker) is gone: every authorized selected pinned document reaches the model completely. Provider composition exhausts pagination before selecting pinned documents.

**Coordination with upstream #26780/#28112:** during review, upstream landed prompt-integrity work touching the same provider seam (`renderPinnedDocuments` now returns `{text, truncated: boolean, includedIds}` and callers expose `pinnedDocumentsTruncated` as the completeness signal, always `false`). This branch concedes that seam wholesale to upstream (100% upstream bytes for `provider.ts` + its two test files) and keeps the complete-injection policy through upstream's own shape. An independent integration review (round 5) verified no silent cap/clip/marker remains, no semantic conflict with #28112's rewritten limit semantics in the auto-merged files, and that no required deliverable was dropped.

Explicit non-goals (follow-up slices of #23103): durable entitlement grants/sharing flows (#23102 coordination), multi-room pin scoping UI.

## What kind of change is this?

Features (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation. (The plugin-documents `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` pair is updated in-branch for the new pin routes.)

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/features/documents/__tests__/actions-pin.test.ts` (agent action wiring), then `plugins/plugin-documents/src/routes.pin.test.ts` (REST + 503 mapping), then `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/document-pin.test.ts` + `plugins/plugin-sql/src/__tests__/integration/document-pin.real.test.ts` (real adapter persistence, CAS + concurrency).

## Detailed testing steps

- Pin/unpin via the DOCUMENT umbrella action; assert metadata-only mutation through existing authorization (never a second write path).
- `POST /api/documents/:id/pin` on a legacy adapter (inherited base method) — expect 503 typed `DOCUMENT_PIN_UNSUPPORTED`, never a fabricated success.
- Concurrent pin toggles on the same document — REAL two-writer SQL proof on PGlite (`document-pin.real.test.ts`): both writers read before either writes, race `Promise.all` CAS writes; exactly one `updated` + one `conflict`, and the loser's retry against fresh state converges. RED control: removing the `expectedPinned` fence makes both writers report `updated` (lost update) and the test fails.
- Pinned provider injection renders complete content (no budget, no marker).

## Runtime contract

Paid/provider dispatch resolves standing before credentials or provider I/O. Warm standing uses exactly one cache read. A cache miss uses one authoritative SQL query and schedules one projection write without reading it back. Denials return a closed safe reason and emit detailed structured no-dispatch context. Post-dispatch ambiguity settles unknown or enters durable reconciliation rather than refunding work that may have been accepted.ac:Tf50,# Relates to

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Defines the exact full five-component restore candidate and staging contract.
- Canonically binds a locator-free verified provider generation, every exact GET completion, the parsed manifest-v3, the lease/catalogue fence, and the final candidate digest.
- Bounds and deeply freezes all receipt ledgers, rejects omitted/duplicate/non-contiguous source slots, and carries explicit source/candidate bindings into one-shot seal authorization.
- Requires atomic authority re-read at authorization/seal and defines strict read-only response-loss replay semantics.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature contract only. No existing caller is switched to it in this PR.

# Documentation changes needed?

N/A — this is an internal, disabled-first contract; user-facing documentation changes begin only when the coordinator is enabled.

ad:Tc9e,## Stack / merge order

This is intentionally stacked on #29766 because both fixes touch the Telegram Worker/gateway boundaries.

## Summary

- make the public Telegram bot identity an explicit environment contract instead of letting inbound webhook auth and outbound bot credentials drift independently
- attest the exact token against the expected bot ID and username with Telegram `getMe` before Worker or gateway traffic can reach typing, turns, delivery ledgers, reply egress, or reminders
- use the homepage bot identity as the production source of truth and a protected, fully distinct staging identity for staging
- enforce the same token, webhook-secret pair, and expected identity across Cloudflare and Railway before release
- add value-free readiness proofs and require them before deployment receipts or Personal Shared edge cutover
- cache only successful, credential-qualified attestations; failures remain fail-closed and redacted

## Verified production behavior

The read-only incident audit confirmed an identity split: onboarding sent users to the canonical public bot, while outbound replies used a stale second bot token. Direct messages to the stale bot did not reach the canonical webhook; replies appeared under the stale identity only when the canonical bot received the inbound message.

This PR makes that state undeployable and prevents either runtime from accepting or sending Telegram traffic under a mismatched identity.

No production or staging secret, webhook, deployment, provider setting, or infrastructure was changed during the audit.

## Safety

- bot ID comparison is exact; username comparison is case-insensitive and otherwise exact
- token-prefix, provider ID, or username mismatch fails before ledger, typing, turn, or egress work
- staging must be fully distinct from production
- attestation errors expose only a bounded reason and retryability, never token-bearing URLs, provider bodies, credentials, or nested causes
- deployment preflights compare protected Worker/Railway values with per-run salted digests and never print the values
- readiness responses contain only project and attested status
- reminder delivery is fenced by the same canonical identity as conversational replies

## Validation

- combined stacked state: 135 focused tests passed, 0 failed
- direct Telegram edge, gateway e2e/forwarding/groups/internal delivery, common attestation, CLI/deploy workflow contracts, and exact-once fallback coverage passed
- API, gateway, common, and Shared typechecks passed; API includes the production Wrangler dry-run
- API/common/gateway lint and `git diff --check` passed
- independent final stacked review reran 127 focused tests with 0 failures and found no blocker, conflict marker, or credential leak

The previous `Source static smoke` failure was the existing `@elizaos/ui` design-contract graph baseline (`4 !== 0` in two checks); neither this PR nor #29766 changes `packages/ui`.

## Summary
- Add one origin-wide Steward session-authority coordinator (Web Lock + durable never-reset logout generation) and route cookie/token mutations through it: session sync, nonce exchange, refresh, callback/restore, passive mirroring, logout, and cookie DELETE.

## Summary

- add one shared paid-proxy route adapter that resolves generative-route standing once and forwards the resulting credential plus admission snapshot into the proxy engine
- classify the paid proxy inventory as route-authenticated so session and API-key callers avoid a global database auth read before the one combined standing decision
- make the rewritten effective Request authoritative for bypass, standing resolution, and execution, including all three query-string API-key RPC variants
- fail closed in production when the Worker lifetime context is absent; explicit local compatibility retains the limiter and never silently dispatches unmetered
- fuse optional strong credential proof into the single durable admission lease and translate typed revocation, warming, and standing denials without provider dispatch
- migrate all 14 paid legacy chain, market, EVM, and Solana routes, the canonical RPC route, and Birdeye through the shared admission path
- preserve typed Solana denial status, code, bounded reason, Retry-After where applicable, and CORS

## Safety contract

- provider dispatch happens only after combined admission succeeds
- session and API-key mounted paths perform exactly one standing cache read and no global user lookup
- denial preserves structured safe reason/logging; warming and unavailable failures are sanitized retryable 503 responses
- combined mode cannot invoke legacy auth or generic reserve
- strong credential proof on and off each acquire exactly one Durable Object admission lease
- settlement remains asynchronous through waitUntil; the response does not wait for projection update and no cache value is read back
- public, read-only, and internal-only routes remain outside this paid adapter

Exact tested head: 0cdf8cebad642bd4718e729bd474937786d99960
Exact base: c1305ba3d8d809743359cb7ef02f20e8f6a36803b0:T54a7,On `develop`, a caller cannot trust complete-retrieval traversal. A document request whose vector recall is empty still comes back carrying keyword-corpus rows that never matched the query. A `plugin-inmemorydb` traversal keeps re-serving page one and then rejects a healthy source. A growing-prefix PII walk aborts a stable source with `ElizaError: PII context memories source changed during traversal`.

Those are the failure classes @lalalune reproduced in #25150. Verbatim:

> 1. Hybrid document search can add irrelevant keyword-corpus rows when vector results are empty or sparse.
> 2. The first-party plugin-inmemorydb adapter does not honor the widened stable offset contract, so complete traversal repeats the first page and rejects healthy sources.
> 3. Growing-prefix PII traversal reranks each prefix with BM25, so a stable source can appear unstable as corpus statistics change.
> 4. Deterministic overlapping document pages can pass double-scan equality while duplicating one row and omitting another.
> 5. Requiring two whole-corpus scans to match rejects ordinary concurrent prepends/appends instead of traversing a stable keyset snapshot.

Refs #25150. **This PR does not close it.** It reproduces all five classes as failing tests and makes them pass, but a CHANGES_REQUESTED review found six defects — four P1 — in the fix itself, and none of them are fixed yet. The per-item dispositions are below; every one is conceded. I am keeping the PR open with the blockers enumerated rather than re-requesting review.

## Review findings — per-item disposition

Against [`startrack3r`'s CHANGES_REQUESTED review](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/28336#pullrequestreview-5016829589) (static review of `9197af5`). I re-read each cited location at `d4b8d5a`. **All six still stand. All six are conceded. None are fixed.**

**1. [P1] RLS principal is bound to a result filter — CONCEDED, OPEN.** `plugins/plugin-sql/src/base.ts:4043` still reads `return this.withEntityContext(params.entityId ?? null, async (tx) => {` inside `searchMemoriesPage`, while `params.entityId` is applied separately as a row filter at the `eq(memoryTable.entityId, params.entityId)` condition. The requester principal is `params.accessContext?.requesterEntityId`. Under PostgreSQL RLS this makes a row filter drive `current_entity_id()`, and an omitted filter supplies no principal at all. The reviewer is also right that the existing real-SQL test uses one UUID for both roles and therefore cannot catch it. Fix owed: bind `withEntityContext` to the validated requester with an explicit absent-context policy, plus real-Postgres cases where requester A filters entity B and where the context is missing or empty.

**2. [P1] Shared in-memory storage is not agent-isolated — CONCEDED, OPEN.** `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:1375` `searchMemoriesPage` filters on `tableName`, `roomId`, `worldId`, `entityId`, and `unique`, with no `memory.agentId === this.agentId` predicate. The plugin shares one `MemoryStorage` across adapters and the dimension rebuild loads every stored agent into the index, and the PII path calls this without an `AccessContext`. Another agent's rows can therefore reach the result, the count, and the snapshot fingerprint. Fix owed: enforce the agent boundary in both the stable and legacy paths, scope index rebuild per agent, and test two adapters sharing one storage across a rebuild.

**3. [P1] This is not storage-level keyset paging — CONCEDED, OPEN, and it is the acceptance criterion.** Confirmed at head: `searchMemoriesPage` issues `.orderBy(asc(distance), desc(memoryTable.createdAt), desc(memoryTable.id))` with no cursor predicate and no `LIMIT`, then filters, maps, and hands the complete ordered corpus to `createStableRetrievalPage`, which slices and fingerprints it in JavaScript. The two document queries do the same. Every page is O(N) transfer, sort, and hash; a traversal is O(N × pages). The prior body disclosed this as a "tradeoff" in *Scope and risk* while ticking the adapter-keyset acceptance box in the same document — that contradiction is withdrawn and the box is now unticked. Fix owed: push the exclusive `(score, createdAt, id)` continuation and the snapshot fence into each adapter query with `LIMIT pageSize + 1`, plus query-shape and large-corpus assertions.

**4. [P1] Torn in-memory storage/index state — CONCEDED, OPEN.** I confirmed at head that `searchMemoriesPage` guards only with `withDocumentMutationLock`, which chains on `documentMutationTail` (`plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:872`). The reviewer's point stands: ordinary create/update/delete write storage and the vector index as separate awaited operations outside that tail, and clearing an embedding leaves the HNSW node behind — I have not independently re-derived that second half. A page can rank against stale vector state, return a differently-shaped stored row, and still mint a snapshot over it. Fix owed: serialize those mutations against stable reads (or publish an atomic immutable snapshot), drop the index node when an embedding is cleared, and add forced-interleaving regressions.

**5. Backward-compatibility regressions — CONCEDED, OPEN, both halves.** (a) `plugins/plugin-inmemorydb/adapter.ts:1320` still has `const threshold = params.match_threshold ?? -1;` on the legacy `searchMemories` path, changing the omitted-threshold default from `0.5` and handing existing callers low- and negative-similarity rows. Restoring `0.5` with tests for omitted / explicit `0` / explicit `-1` is owed. (b) `packages/core/src/types/runtime.ts:644,647` declare `searchMemoriesPage` and `rerankMemories` as required `IAgentRuntime` members while the runtime feature-detects them as optional — that breaks structurally typed third-party runtimes. Owed: model them as optional or versioned capability members, or move them to an extended interface.

**6. Stable-helper cross-adapter gaps — CONCEDED, OPEN.** Confirmed at head in `packages/core/src/database/stable-retrieval.ts`: `buildSnapshot` compares `key.id > upperId` as a raw case-sensitive string while the canonical adapter comparator lowercases to match PostgreSQL, and `fingerprint()` hashes only `id`, `createdAt`, `similarity`, `content`, `embedding`, `metadata`, `roomId`, `worldId`, `entityId` — so a mutation to a returned field it omits, such as `unique`, passes the old snapshot unchanged. Owed: canonicalize UUID comparison and duplicate identity, fingerprint the complete canonical returned row, and add parity/mutation tests.

**7. Overstated end-to-end claim — CONCEDED and corrected here.** The reviewer is right that the projection case is not the real end-to-end path the previous body advertised. `packages/core/src/security/issue-25150-runtime-adversarial.test.ts:124` constructs a real `DocumentService`, but the adapter beneath it is `queryDocumentFragments: vi.fn(async () => fragments)` over 1,205 synthetic rows, with a mocked runtime around it. It proves the projection seam does not silently truncate; it does not prove a real DocumentService → storage → planner path. The "real `DocumentService` → projection → `AgentRuntime` dispatch" wording is withdrawn.

**8. Evidence-row markers — FIXED.** All seven mandatory evidence-row markers plus the OCR row were missing from the previous body and are restored below, and the evidence-head marker now carries `d4b8d5a`.

**9. Rebase onto live `develop` — PARTIALLY DONE.** Rebased onto `f2ccf25` at `d4b8d5a`, preserving both sides of the `plugin-inmemorydb` conflict with #28112 (`const limit = params.count ?? params.limit;` from develop, `const threshold = params.match_threshold ?? -1;` from this PR — and per finding 5 that second line is itself owed a revert). `develop` has since advanced 6 commits; another rebase is owed.

- [ ] **Not met.** Every first-party adapter implements the same stable ordered keyset/cursor contract — the *cursor semantics* are enforced and ignored cursors are rejected, but per finding 3 the SQL adapters do not issue a keyset query; they materialize the full corpus and page it in JavaScript.

- [ ] **Partially met.** Stable snapshot contract tolerating concurrent appends or returning a typed conflict — `RETRIEVAL_SNAPSHOT_CONFLICT` with `action: restart-from-first-page` works for the tested vectors, but findings 4 and 6 mean the snapshot can be minted over torn in-memory state and can miss mutations to unfingerprinted fields.

- [ ] **Overstated, corrected.** Integrate with #24592 so complete retrieval cannot later be hidden by prompt projection — the projection seam is covered over a mocked adapter (finding 7), not the real retrieval path.
- [ ] **Not met.** Focused tests, typecheck/build/lint, root verify, exact-head CI, and independent review pass — focused tests, biome and typecheck pass at `d4b8d5a`; root `verify`, builds and lints are stale at `9197af5`; exact-head CI is red; the independent review is CHANGES_REQUESTED and unanswered in code.

## Scope and risk

Risk: medium, and higher than the previous body admitted. `IDatabaseAdapter` / `IAgentRuntime` gain stable-page methods and a capability marker; findings 1, 2 and 5 mean the current shape of those additions changes an authorization principal, crosses an agent boundary, and moves a public default. Legacy adapters take the corrected single-rerank path; first-party adapters take the native contract.

Snapshot verification fingerprints the complete fenced authorized corpus on every page. That makes mutation detection deterministic and is why the tests pass, but it is O(N × pages) over a traversal and is exactly what finding 3 rejects. No scalability improvement is claimed anywhere in this PR.

No documentation change is required: this changes the database/runtime contract and its exported public types, not operator-facing setup.

b5:Ta2a,## What changed

- diagnose the exact failed Dedicated canary across its Docker process, Tailscale socket, Headscale REST inventory, tags, route, and active peer identity without exposing private addresses or credentials
- select the unique canonical tailnet IPv4 from Headscale's unordered repeated address field instead of assuming address zero is IPv4
- retain the exact observed Headscale node ID in the replacement cleanup locator before Docker/Headscale address binding, so a mismatch cannot strand an offline peer or poison the next deterministic-name provision
- lock both behaviors with real integration/provider-path regressions

## Why

Fresh signed-in Dedicated canary `33712952322` reached a running agent process and registered an exact tagged Headscale peer, but provisioning still reported missing ingress. Follow-up diagnostics proved the API/CLI peer existed and that its assigned peer address differed from the stale database observation. The provider then dropped the observed node ID when final address binding failed; Docker cleanup proceeded while the Headscale identity remained orphaned.

Headscale's v0.28 node contract exposes `ip_addresses` as a repeated field and does not promise IPv4-first ordering. Treating element zero as the routable IPv4 turns a valid IPv6-first registration into a false registration miss. The repaired selector accepts exactly one canonical CGNAT IPv4 and fails closed on zero or ambiguity.

Closes the remaining registration-settlement and orphan-cleanup defects tracked in #29341.

b8:T8c6,## Summary

This PR adds `@elizaos/plugin-technocore`, an official plugin integrating **elizaOS autonomous agents** directly with the **Technocore decentralized agent protocol** (`technocore.chat`).

### Features:
1. **Autonomous & Deterministic Cryptographic Identity**: Auto-generates or deterministically loads 32-byte Ed25519 seed (`TECHNOCORE_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX`) deriving standard `did:key:z...` multicodec identities (`0xed01` base58btc).
2. **Decentralized Messaging Actions**:
   - `TECHNOCORE_POST_MESSAGE`: Cryptographically signs and broadcasts messages with strictly monotonic nanosecond nonces.
   - `TECHNOCORE_READ_ROOM`: Chronological message stream reader with pagination.
   - `TECHNOCORE_LIST_ROOMS`: Active room discovery across the decentralized mesh.
3. **Decentralized Persistent Memory Actions**:
   - `TECHNOCORE_KV_SET` / `TECHNOCORE_KV_GET`: Reconciled persistent key-value memory (`/kv/eliza-agent/latest`).

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`#25372` made billing cancellation commands and their key aliases immutable audit/idempotency receipts. Their restrictive organization, user, and job references now prevent terminal personal-account deletion.

This PR preserves those receipts while independently anonymizing:

- organization ownership together with the transitive job reference; and
- the historical requesting user, including actors that later moved organizations.

Only the exact leased/calling database-erasure phase, request generation, and irreversible lifecycle rows can perform the one-way detach. Keys are locked and updated before commands in ascending UUID order. A direct command FK and deferred key/command organization-proof constraint prevent drift after the original composite FK becomes NULL-vacuous.

The four direct billing receipt relationships are classified as `anonymize_retained_record`; the receipts themselves are never deleted.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and database integrity improvement.

# Documentation changes needed?

No user-facing documentation change is required. Migration and runtime invariants are documented in code and tests.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

The manual staging identity run [32934061930](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/32934061930) concluded successfully even though it emitted only `database identity report unavailable` and produced no receipt. The standalone CLI caught the unavailable result and returned exit code 0.

This patch introduces a testable standalone reporter boundary that:

- returns `1` when `DATABASE_URL` is missing, connection/query work is unavailable, result publication fails, or the report result is `unavailable`;
- returns `0` after successfully publishing `reported`, `mismatch`, or `match` evidence;
- keeps all diagnostics generic and closes any created client in `finally`;
- uses `process.exitCode` to avoid force-exiting after the reporter and teardown settle;
- leaves `runDatabaseIdentityPreflight` and every migration call site unchanged.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix: removes a false-success diagnostic result without changing database or release mutation policy.

# Documentation changes needed?

No documentation change is required. The existing runbook already defines the standalone command as a receipt-preparation tool and migration `report` as non-blocking; this patch makes the standalone exit status match that documented purpose.

be:T69c,Closes #30635

Paid provider calls previously required separate Durable Object requests to acquire a billing lease and mark provider dispatch. This change commits both atomically immediately before provider invocation, removing one network round trip while preserving standing checks, revocation ordering, and durable settlement.

The optimization covers chat completions, messages, embeddings, media generation, voice, MCP/A2A, shared runtime chat, and the generic proxy engine. Standing retains one cache read with asynchronous projection updates and no reread. Provider and dedicated proxy failures include validated trace IDs and sanitized upstream request IDs where available.

Retries reuse a cancellation capability. Both lost acknowledgements and requests that never reach the Durable Object are covered: failures before provider execution settle zero, definitive denials create no lease, and ambiguous release treats only the specific missing-lease response as idempotent. Legacy endpoints remain compatible during rolling deployments.

Validation: focused provider and admission suites passed; API/shared typechecks, 709 mounted route contracts, production Worker dry-run, formatting, and root `bun run verify` passed (376/376 tasks plus repository audits). GitHub run 33979069995 passed every required check for commit 13b9d84028bf0c4a1d402f8919279cf2458091b8, including PostgreSQL authority constraints and billing replay E2E.

The deterministic benchmark proves one billing Durable Object fetch before provider work. Prior staging measurements attributed roughly 20–25 ms to the removed hop; deployed latency certification remains required to establish the actual improvement.
bf:T10e0,Dedicated activation now waits for its provisioning job before cutting over to the new backend. Fresh activation requires a nonempty job ID, adoption retains its own job identity, and terminal failures stop the transition with an actionable error. Pending work and response-body reads share an absolute deadline.

Worker provisioning nudges are retained through `executionCtx.waitUntil`; hosts without that context await the work. Shared history that is still warming returns a retryable `503 shared_history_unavailable`. Exact auth-token and pending-greetings bootstrap routes avoid unrelated initialization. Privacy-safe cutover diagnostics retain the latest machine code and status.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Keeps Google OWNER and AGENT grants for the same Google subject isolated with a
  provider-owned, role-scoped account key.
- Makes `(agent, provider, externalId, role)` the active SQL natural identity.
- Lazily upgrades legacy rows without changing their UUIDs or credential refs.
- Rejects ambiguous aliases, external identity mutation, and role collisions
  before provider side effects.
- Serializes OAuth completion for the same agent/provider within one process,
  including final writes and compensation.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking change).

## Why are we doing this? Any context or related work?

The Google role split introduced in #26723 computed role-bound logical IDs, but
the database bridge still persisted the raw external subject as `accountKey`.
That collapsed OWNER and AGENT grants back onto one connector account.

# Documentation changes needed?

No project documentation change is required. The provider/storage contract and
migration behavior are documented in code and regression tests.

# Risks

Medium cloud-provider boundary change. Incorrect validation or action settlement can create orphan resources, report deletion before provider completion, or hide a provider error. The implementation therefore validates before transport, binds every returned action to one deadline, and requires exact readback/absence proof.

# What this PR does

- validates positive safe Hetzner server identities before any create-volume request;
- sends exactly one volume placement selector (`server` or `location`) and preserves both `automount: true` and `automount: false`;
- validates and settles create action plus every `next_actions` entry under one operation deadline before exact readback;
- keeps request abort deadlines active through response-body read and parse;
- settles server-delete `action` and `next_actions` before proving exact target absence;
- accepts the official volume-delete 204 response while also validating and settling a complete JSON action envelope when supplied;
- distinguishes target 404 idempotence from action-poll 404 failure;
- makes the local Hetzner mock enforce the provider placement contract and exercise the real client over HTTP.

# Scope boundary

This PR does not migrate or unquarantine legacy metadata-only nodes; modify capacity, bootstrap, maintenance, availability, or SSH/filesystem consumers; change volume attach/detach authority; or implement provisioning compensation. Those remain explicit work in #22916. No live provider call was made.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces duplicate synchronous/shell Git readers with one complete async reader; uses NUL-delimited filename protocols. A real 10.7 MB change previously lost its final marker while reporting `truncated:false`; Unicode paths previously pointed to nonexistent files.
- Validates analysis document identity and results-map shape before merging. Arrays and mismatched subjects fail without replacing original bytes; arbitrary analyzer IDs are stored as own data properties.
- Disposes the idle worker's abort listener on normal timer expiry and handles already-aborted signals immediately.
- Replaces two 16,000-character event-payload cutoff helpers with a scheduling-owned JSON boundary; persistence, retry/escalation and final prompt assembly retain complete event data. Unsupported data fails before task claim.
- Makes widget execution errors nonzero, clears old output, and reuses local fixture/Tailwind helpers instead of a CDN and fixed wait. Completed widget findings retain the existing `FAIL_ON_VIOLATIONS` policy.
- Moves byte-identical finance/health token encryption into a Node-only shared subpath, retaining plugin compatibility exports and old envelopes.
- Removes 13 unregistered/unexported voice-profile prototype files, including fabricated diarization and a 617-line self-contained role “integration” suite. Live voice-profile persistence remains in local-inference.

## What kind of change is this?

Behavioral bug fixes, consolidation, and removal of unused code. 44 files; net 749 lines removed including tests and compatibility adapters.

c4:T3018,The shared native Fetch path now preserves RequestInit overrides and cancellation through body consumption. App-core uses the UI-owned iOS transport and singleton state, and simultaneous watchdog events coalesce into one native start request. A failed streaming request propagates its error after dispatch, so an already accepted POST cannot be replayed through the buffered bridge.

Android applies the same no-replay contract. The resolver reads Capacitor's native method metadata because its JavaScript proxy can expose a streaming function that an older bridge does not implement. Bridges without that capability select buffered compatibility before dispatch. Real Android native integration reproduces two accepted POSTs and misleading success with the old code; the fixed path accepts one POST, reports the failure, and removes its listeners. An actual native legacy-capability fixture confirms one buffered request through the public resolver.

## What this adds

`packages/core/src/messaging/interactions/sessions.ts` exported three surfaces with no test coverage anywhere on `develop`:

- `applyMessageInteractionClaim` — the pure atomic claim transition, including lease acquisition, identical-lease `in_progress`, expired-lease `resumed` with attempt increment, digest comparison against claimed/committed/completed states, preset-response tampering refusal, binding mismatch, revocation/expiry refusal while pending, reference/clock/TTL validation;
- `validateMessageInteractionResponse` — object/array rejection, unexpected-field and missing-required-field (named from schema fields) rejection, boolean/finite-number/UTF-8-byte-limit enforcement, option membership including number-to-string matching, and media-capability URL / byte / MIME validation for attachments;
- `responseSchemaForInteraction` — choice options vs `allowCustom`, text-like byte capping against `maxTextResponseBytes` (non-text fields keep their own bound), secret-field refusal outside the sensitive flow, followups-to-payload mapping, task acknowledgement shape.

The suite also covers the callback encode/decode pair (round-trip plus every malformed shape), the store-level branches not exercised by the existing API-level suite (duplicate-reference collision, clone isolation, double-commit refusal, concurrent claim serialization, `listCommitted` time/limit/ordering, `deleteExpired` per-terminal-state timestamps), and an authority end-to-end run proving exactly-once execution: a second consume of the same replay key replays the retained receipt without re-running the effect executor.

It complements the existing `session-authority.test.ts`, which drives the store and authority APIs; the pure transition functions and validators were previously reachable only through that narrower surface.

## What changed

- Adds one shared standing-only paid-route guard that reuses the combined inference identity decision.
- A warm request performs the existing single combined cache read. A cold request awaits and consumes the authoritative continuation directly without rereading the cache.
- Standing denials preserve bounded safe reasons, emit route-bound structured diagnostics with providerDispatched=false, and stop before durable claims, debits, credentials, or provider dispatch.
- Applies the guard to R2 list/presign/object operations, Tailscale auth-key creation, remote host enrollment with optional Headscale provisioning, domain purchase, and credential-broker user OAuth calls.
- Keeps existing synchronous receipt, lease, debit, refund, and reconciliation behavior intact.

## Deliberate exemptions

- Credential refresh/revalidation remains available as an authentication recovery operation.
- Remote host token recovery and revocation/cleanup remain available while new work is fenced.
- Remote host listing and domain status/check/reconciliation reads remain read-only/recovery paths.
- Signed one-use managed-network activation and blob capability reads retain their delegated proof and do not add a second account-cache read.
- MCP provider proxy already uses the generative standing guard and is not double-admitted.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces Billing's indefinite signed-out skeleton with an explicit sign-in state wired to the Settings host login flow.
- Distinguishes auth resolution, query pending/error/paused/freshness, unavailable-user, and content states instead of rendering cached data as current.
- Keys invoice cache entries by organization so switching tenants cannot paint the previous organization's invoice.
- Gives sign-in and retry actions agent-operable descriptors and correct busy/disabled behavior.
- Applies the same freshness rules to the invoice detail route.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No. This restores the intended runtime contract and adds user-facing strings through the existing i18n catalog.

ca:Tacd,## Summary

- add a manual, staging-only Smart Placement vs default-placement certification workflow
- require both pre-provisioned arms to serve one exact develop SHA
- read Cloudflare placement status before and after the window and fail if the treatment is not `smart` or the control is not default
- hash the arms' sanitized binding topology so a control with divergent Durable Object, Hyperdrive, KV, R2, rate-limit, variable, or secret-binding structure cannot be compared
- collect at least 30 successful concurrent warm pairs plus cold/post-idle controls, with p50/p90/p95 stratified by observed `cf-placement`
- retain no prompts, generated text, keys, response bodies, or secret values
- document the operator-owned control-arm provisioning and cleanup prerequisites

Refs #30099.

## Why no direct placement change

The exact-SHA staging certification at `be86906a83d633587078ecc3cceca6d453463101` ([run 33326096912](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/33326096912)) recorded 22/22 gateway responses as `cf-placement=remote-LAX` from ORD ingress. Eleven successful warm samples had gateway preforward p50 322 ms and p90 571 ms; the phase p50s were auth 71 ms, middle 85 ms, reserve 83 ms, and setup 77 ms.

A read-only Workers service query reported staging Smart Placement `SUCCESS`, confirming LAX is the active fetch-handler placement decision. It does not reveal Durable Object location. Cloudflare documents that existing Durable Objects do not relocate, while this monolithic Worker also uses Hyperdrive and external inference providers. Disabling placement without a same-SHA control would trade one unknown against another.

## Safety boundary

This PR does not deploy, create, edit, route, or delete a Worker. It rejects production origins and Worker names. The account currently has no placement-control Worker, so the workflow cannot run until an operator explicitly authorizes and provisions a staging-only control with external bindings to the canonical Durable Object namespaces and identical staging resources/secrets.

## What changed

- removes the isolate-local inference refusal map that could reject a healthy request after an asynchronous settlement or projection failure; the revision-aware organization Durable Object remains the admission authority
- removes the duplicate app-settlement balance projection invalidation while preserving fail-closed repair semantics
- adds safe top-level HTTP status evidence and bounded child-failure diagnostics to the latency certification harness
- records browser-literal adoption request and exact provisioning-job lifecycle timing without serializing job identifiers
- preserves the original typed Dedicated provisioning failure cause through retry settlement
- adds trace IDs, phase timing, and structured internal failures to the Dedicated adoption boundary while keeping public errors sanitized

## Why

The paired staging trace isolated a transient 503 to a redundant isolate-local refusal fast path. Warm successful calls showed roughly 74 ms before provider forwarding: about 3 ms standing cache, 25 ms organization rate-limit DO, 26 ms balance lease DO, and 21 ms dispatch marker DO. Cerebras response headers were roughly 75 ms, close to direct calls. This patch removes the incorrect extra authority and makes the remaining Cloudflare, adoption, and provider boundaries directly diagnosable.

# Risk

**Medium.** This changes one-time SSO code custody, exchange finalization, local token publication, cookie synchronization, and logout ordering. A regression could strand a login, publish a stale token, navigate after a superseding exchange, or recreate a session after logout.

The implementation keeps the API contract narrow, serializes same-realm finalization, bounds cookie synchronization, and adds deterministic tests for StrictMode, unmount, state changes, out-of-order responses, stale persistence, navigation failure, cookie ordering, and logout races.

# What does this PR do?

It hardens both legs of the cloud SSO bridge.

1. **Abandoned mint custody**
   - Burns a minted one-time code exactly once if the route unmounts, changes authorization state, or cannot hand off.
   - Adds a sessionless, destruction-only `POST /burn` endpoint restricted to exact bridge origins.
   - Keeps successful handoff and StrictMode replay single-shot.

2. **Generation-safe exchange and recovery**
   - Consumes state/verifier once and ignores late results from superseded route generations.
   - Prevents stale exchanges from publishing a token or navigating.
   - Serializes token publication and server-cookie synchronization so the newest valid exchange wins.
   - Makes cookie synchronization abortable and bounded to 10 seconds.
   - Orders logout/account-switch teardown with exchange finalization and prevents any session POST from starting after a concurrent logout.
   - Recovers from rejected bridge redirects instead of leaving the app or join page on a permanent spinner.

The same-realm browser contract is covered. Cross-tab/cross-realm coordination is not claimed; the generation queue, abort controller, and logout epoch are module-local.

# Review guide

Start with:

- `packages/ui/src/cloud/sso-bridge/SsoBridgeRoute.tsx`
- `packages/ui/src/cloud/sso-bridge/sso-bridge.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/steward-session-client/index.ts`
- Their adjacent tests

Important invariants:

- Before the guarded persistence commit point, a superseded exchange writes and emits nothing.
- Once a valid persistence begins, later valid generations are ordered after it and the newest one wins.
- A stale generation never navigates.
- Logout wins over an exchange still waiting on persistence or cookie synchronization.
- The burn endpoint remains destruction-only and exposes no validity oracle.

# What changed

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds a caller job with no GitHub Environment that reduces the two effective
  repository/organization Telegram variables to one boolean provenance result.
- Passes that result through a required typed reusable-workflow input because a
  reusable call cannot consume the caller job's `vars` context directly.
- Makes the Environment-scoped staging preflight reject any outer-scope
  authority before migration, API deployment, or Pages mutation, then validates
  the complete staging-Environment pair.
- Keeps production source-canonical and ignores every GitHub Telegram input.
- Executes the actual preflight shell across success, conflict, malformed,
  cross-environment, and production matrices without exposing configured values.
- Updates workflow, application, and homepage operator documentation to describe
  the exact authority and admission order.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking): release-policy hardening for the staging Telegram public
identity.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation changes are required and included. Workflow guidance, both
byte-identical homepage package guides, the homepage README, and local `.env`
examples now describe GitHub Environment staging authority and source-canonical
production behavior.

## Deployment instructions

N/A for this PR - no deployment is part of the code review. Follow the remaining
authorized steps in #29206 after merge.de:T1d42,# What

Regenerating the action-search keywords **destroys committed translations**. Running the repo's own `generate:action-search-keywords` on current `develop` adds the 4 missing entries it should — and silently drops **16 committed terms across 15 key/locale pairs**:

| entry | locale | term lost |
|---|---|---|
| `action.file.request` | es / ko / pt / tl / vi / zh-CN | `escribir archivo`, `쓰기 파일`, `escrever arquivo`, `isulat file`, `viết tệp`, `写入 文件` |
| `action.runtimes.request` | es / ko / pt / tl / vi / zh-CN | `token`, `토큰`, `token`, `token`, `tao`, `代币` + `令牌` |
| `action.views.request` | ko / tl / zh-CN | `쓰기`, `isulat`, `写入` |

`base` loses nothing — #22402's pinning from f0d4c39d9 works, but **only for `base`**. Every loss is in a locale.

So "the artifact is stale" was not something you could fix by running the generator. That's what this PR fixes first.

# Two independent causes

**1. `buildLocaleTerms` translated `base.slice(0, 64)`** — a positional window over an alphabetically sorted, *growing* list. In `action.file.request`, `write file` sat at base index 59; the regen's new terms pushed it to 67, out of the window, so all six of its localized forms stopped being derivable. Nothing about term 65 makes it less worth translating than term 64 — `64` was the only bare numeric limit in the file (`BASE_LIMIT`/`LOCALE_LIMIT` are named constants) and had no comment. **10 of the 16 losses come from this, all of them below the locale cap.**

**2. The locale lists never pinned `existing[locale]`.** `base` uses `limitTermsPinned`; each locale used plain `limitTerms`, so committed terms were re-scored against fresh candidates and evicted at `LOCALE_LIMIT`. This is precisely the bug f0d4c39d9 describes, on the code path it didn't cover. **The remaining 6 losses, all at the 48-term cap.**

# The change

```js
-  for (const term of base.slice(0, 64)) {
+  for (const term of base) {
```
```js
-    const deduped = limitTerms(dedupeTerms(terms), LOCALE_LIMIT);
+    const deduped = limitTermsPinned(
+      dedupeTerms(arrayValue(existing[locale])),
+      dedupeTerms(terms),
+      LOCALE_LIMIT,
+    );
```

That was `limitTerms`' last caller, so it's removed (biome flagged it).

# Both edits are load-bearing, and the window fix is *not* safe alone

| variant | committed terms lost | terms gained |
|---|---|---|
| `develop` (neither) | **16** | +81 |
| window fix only | **129** | +287 |
| pin fix only | **0** | +76 |
| **both (this PR)** | **0** | **+158** |

Translating all of `base` floods the 48-slot candidate list, so on its own it makes eviction **eight times worse**. It's only safe once the committed terms are pinned. Applied together the regen becomes purely additive: **0 lost, +158 gained, 4 entries added, 0 removed.**

I'll flag a claim I had to drop: I first justified the window fix by arguing the new `action.channelRecap.request` (base length 68) would ship with a truncated translation set. Measured, it has 140 localized terms in all four variants — that argument was wrong. The window fix earns its place on different evidence: **+82 localized terms across 9 entries** (`browser`, `liquidity`, `logs`, `oauth`, `payment`, `room`, `scheduledTasks`, `wallet`, …), with none removed.

# The 4 entries the regen adds

All four actions are shipped and had **no search keywords in any of the 7 locales**:

| action | defined at |
|---|---|
| `CALCULATE` | `packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/actions/calculate.ts:247` |
| `CHANNEL_RECAP` | `packages/core/src/features/basic-capabilities/actions/channel-recap.ts:96` |
| `FAMILY_WORKFLOWS` | `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/family-workflows.ts:14` |
| `OWNER_AGREEMENT_KNOWLEDGE` | `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/agreement-knowledge.ts:59` |

# Why not `action-search-overrides.keywords.json`

I checked whether the curated terms belong in the overrides file instead. `generate-keywords.mjs` merges every `*.keywords.json` in the directory, so that would work mechanically — but overrides holds one entry of hand-authored phrasing the audit cannot derive (`server template`, `guild management`, …), and none of the lost terms. These terms *are* dictionary-derived generator output; f0d4c39d9 chose to pin rather than relocate them for exactly this reason, and this follows that precedent.

e1:Te73,
## What this adds

Gandr as a voice synthesis provider in the cloud TTS route (`POST /api/v1/voice/tts`), wired the same way as the Cartesia lane.

- New `packages/cloud/api/v1/voice/tts/gandr-synthesis.ts` beside `cartesia-synthesis.ts`. Gandr speaks the OpenAI `/v1/audio/speech` contract over plain HTTPS, so there is no WebSocket adapter to drive. The MP3 lane is one POST with the response body streamed through. The WAV lane requests `response_format: "pcm"` (headerless s16le mono 24000 Hz), drains it under the existing byte cap, and wraps it with the shared pcm16 helpers for codec-less clients.
- Provider selection: explicit `gandr-*` voice ids (`gandr-mia`, `gandr-ava`, `gandr-jenny`, `gandr-dane`, `gandr-leo`, `gandr-lewis`) route to Gandr when `GANDR_API_KEY` is set. Unknown `gandr-*` shaped ids fail with 400 and known ids without a key fail with 503, the same fail-closed shape the Kokoro lane uses, so a typo never waits on or bills through another upstream.
- Gandr never substitutes for an unpinned default. With no `gandr-*` voice id in the request, behavior is unchanged: Cartesia default, Kokoro free fallback, ElevenLabs custom voices, all exactly as before.
- Route: same response shapes as the Cartesia lane (streamed MP3, buffered WAV), same typed error taxonomy (`GandrRestTtsError` with rate_limit/quota/auth/bad_request/provider_unavailable), same billing lane (charges the existing ElevenLabs catalog rate; usage records attribute `synthesisEngine: "gandr"`, model `tts-1`). The first-line MP3 cache is keyed per provider so Gandr entries can never collide with Cartesia or ElevenLabs entries, and the background populate re-synthesizes the snip with Gandr, never with a different engine.
- Gandr accepts up to 2000 characters per request while the route-wide cap is 5000. The route rejects the overage on the Gandr lane with an explicit 400 (`gandr_text_too_long`) instead of truncating.
- Env: one new optional var, `GANDR_API_KEY`, documented in `cloud-worker-env.ts`. Nothing changes when it is unset.
- Tests: `__tests__/gandr-synthesis.test.ts` covers the request shape, bearer auth, MP3 stream passthrough, 24 kHz WAV wrapping, the typed 429 error, and the overflow and empty-body throws. `provider-selection.test.ts` gains cases for the explicit lane, the fail-closed paths, and a regression that defaults never move to Gandr.

## Render evidence

A live smoke run of this PR's Gandr lane rendered two files through the plugin code path, not a mock:

- MP3 lane: `gandr-eliza-proof.mp3`, 58,368 bytes, valid MP3 header (ff f3 c4). Request: `model: tts-1`, voice `alloy`, `response_format: mp3`.
- PCM lane: `gandr-eliza-proof.pcm`, 168,978 bytes, 84,489 s16le frames at 24000 Hz, 3.52 seconds. Request: the same with `response_format: pcm`, drained by the pcm16 stub and wrapped with the shared helpers.

The plugin's own log line during the PCM render:

```
[Voice TTS API] Gandr WAV synthesis {"totalMs":2026,"wavBytes":168978}
```

Both artifacts and the run notes are attached to a release on the fork for inspection: https://github.com/AALG123/eliza/releases/tag/gandr-render-evidence-20260830

## About Gandr

Gandr is a text-to-speech API with an OpenAI compatible endpoint (`POST https://tts.gandr.ai/v1/audio/speech`, bearer auth). Six voices, 23 languages. Every render is watermarked. First audio byte in 146 ms over the open internet, 116 ms p50 first audio, server side warm. Keys at https://gandr.ai; the free tier is 50,000 tokens.

Disclosure: I work on Gandr.

Checks run before filing: `tsc -p packages/cloud/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors in any file this PR touches, and `bun test` on the two test files passes 19 of 19.

Closes #22535.

## Regression Protected

The existing Cloud audit fixture always returned Dedicated, so it could not detect a regression where Shared disappears early, destructive controls leak onto Shared, activation sends the wrong quote, retryable cutover stops after the first 409, Dedicated fails to supersede Shared, or zero-credit silently mutates the agent. Existing route snapshots and component tests do not own this browser-level transition across responsive layouts.

</li>
<li>
<p><a href="https://redirect.github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11515">#11515</a> <a href="https://github.com/biomejs/biome/commit/382b15d5e0f9e2a75604fec1f15ad342628c99c7"><code>382b15d</code></a> Thanks <a href="https://github.com/dyc3"><code>@​dyc3</code></a>! - Fixed <a href="https://redirect.github.com/biomejs/biome/issues/11390">#11390</a>, where <code>noFloatingPromises</code> performed expensive full type inference for calls to non-Promise methods declared on third-party TypeScript classes. The rule now classifies those calls using targeted type information.</p>

<li>
<p><a href="https://redirect.github.com/biomejs/biome/pull/11516">#11516</a> <a href="https://github.com/biomejs/biome/commit/6f40e8224afc58737626d997c0ea779e2b37baca"><code>6f40e82</code></a> Thanks <a href="https://github.com/levrik"><code>@​levrik</code></a>! - Fixed <a href="https://biomejs.dev/linter/rules/no-vue-ref-as-operand/"><code>noVueRefAsOperand</code></a> so it no longer reports a callback parameter (e.g. from <code>.find()</code>, <code>.map()</code>) as an unwrapped ref value just because it's nested inside a <code>ref()</code>, <code>computed()</code>, or similar call.</p>

Updates `@vitejs/plugin-react` from 6.0.5 to 6.1.1
<details>
<summary>Release notes</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/releases">@​vitejs/plugin-react's releases</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<h2>plugin-react@6.1.1</h2>
<h3>Add <code>compiler.logDiagnostics</code> option</h3>
<p>Recoverable React Compiler diagnostics are no longer logged by default. Set <code>compiler.logDiagnostics</code> to <code>true</code> to log them through Vite. Fatal diagnostics are always logged and fail the transform.</p>
<h3>Respect environment sourcemap option for React Compiler transform when <code>builder.sharedPlugins</code> is enabled (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/pull/1439">#1439</a>)</h3>
<p>The React Compiler transform was using the top-level sourcemap option instead of the environment sourcemap option. This caused a problem when the experimental <code>builder.sharedPlugins</code> was enabled.</p>
<h2>plugin-react@6.1.0</h2>
<h3>Add experimental native React Compiler support (<a href="https://redirect.github.com/vitejs/vite-plugin-react/pull/1419">#1419</a>)</h3>
<p>Add experimental native React Compiler support.</p>
<p>You can use it by installing <code>oxc-transform-react</code> and enabling it via the <code>compiler</code> option:</p>
<pre lang="sh"><code>npm install -D oxc-transform-react
</code></pre>
<pre lang="js"><code>import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
<p>export default defineConfig({<br />
plugins: [<br />
react({ compiler: true })<br />
]<br />
})<br />
</code></pre></p>
</blockquote>
</details>
